claims.claim: Hydroponic / indoor-grown lettuce is priced at a premium over conventionally grown product at retail.
claims.episode_span: The finished head of lettuce reaches the store at prices several times higher than field-grown equivalents, even though the seeds and water involved remain inexpensive commodities.
claims.source_title: Behind the greens: Why hydroponic lettuce is not competitive yet - AgFunderNews
claims.supporting_quote: Hydroponic and locally grown product is priced at a premium, even versus organic.

claims.claim: Current specific energy consumption for lettuce in indoor vertical farms is about 10-18 kWh per kilogram (total).
claims.episode_span: Total electricity use commonly runs 10–18 kWh per kilogram of fresh produce in reported installations, with lighting the largest share and cooling and dehumidification most of the remainder.
claims.source_title: Solve Vertical Farming Energy Problem: 5 Real Solutions (verticalfarming.blog)
claims.supporting_quote: current specific energy consumption for lettuce production in indoor vertical farms at 10–18 kWh per kilogram

claims.claim: Field-grown lettuce uses roughly 1-5 kWh/kg of (almost entirely indirect) energy, far below vertical-farm figures.
claims.episode_span: Field agriculture, by contrast, receives its photons at zero direct cost and sheds heat to the open air, so its cost structure never encounters this double burden.
claims.source_title: Solve Vertical Farming Energy Problem: 5 Real Solutions (verticalfarming.blog)
claims.supporting_quote: In a traditional open field, the equivalent figure is 1–5 kWh/kg – almost entirely indirect energy (machinery, fertilizer, irrigation).

claims.claim: Lettuce is about 94.9 percent water, so nearly all of a head's mass is water rather than dry matter.
claims.episode_span: A typical head of lettuce contains on the order of a few tens of grams of dry matter, mostly carbohydrates and water, whose commodity value as bulk biomass is measured in cents.
claims.supporting_quote: The high water content of lettuce (94.9 percent) creates problems when attempting to preserve the plant

claims.claim: A theoretical future benchmark of 3.1-7.4 kWh/kg has been identified for vertical-farm lettuce, well below current reported energy use.
claims.episode_span: combined with published energy-use figures per kilogram that fall well below the current reported range.
claims.source_title: Solve Vertical Farming Energy Problem: 5 Real Solutions (verticalfarming.blog)
claims.supporting_quote: The same study identifies a theoretical future benchmark of 3.1–7.4 kWh/kg as the direction technology is moving
